name: Chisel
text: Run the 10-video blind accuracy test now. If the error rate stays under 5%, adopt kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript for all pending videos. name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t editors wasting hours *after* the test—it’s YouTube’s raw transcript changing mid-stream *during* the test, invalidating the 5% threshold before we even start. Lock the 10-video sample set in policy *now* with timestamps, then run the test once. That settles it: no adoption until the artifact (locked sample set + test results) exists.

name: Scope

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t the test’s outcome—it’s locking editors into a tool that fails *after* bulk processing starts. Instead, run the 10-video blind test *on the next batch only*, then adopt the tool if it meets the 5% threshold. That settles it: the artifact is the test results for the next batch, not a policy lock.

name: Reel
text: Run the 10-video blind accuracy test now using kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtu. name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t editors wasting hours *before* the test—they’re already wasting hours *now* with YouTube’s raw transcripts. Lock the test to 10 videos, but run it against *both* the raw YouTube output *and* the tool’s output in parallel, blind-reviewed by two editors. The artifact is the comparative error-rate table. If the tool’s error rate is within 2% of raw YouTube’s, adopt it immediately—no 5% threshold delay.
